items.title: Table maintenance service
items.summary: Snapshot expiry, orphan-file removal, data-file compaction and manifest rewrites per table, on a schedule and on demand, with retention as a table property
items.done: A table with 1,000 small files and 100 snapshots is compacted and expired on schedule. Time travel within retention still works, orphaned files are gone, and every action is audited
items.note: policies per table, schema or default; compaction, snapshot expiry, orphan removal on a schedule; automatic clustering: sort columns chosen from what the table's queries filter on (Trino's query history), the sort order set and the files rewritten when they overlap (tests/test_trino_e2e.py)

items.title: Governed Spark on restricted tables
items.summary: A policy-enforcing scan path for masks and row filters (Spark Connect on trusted compute, or a Cairn-planned scan through Trino), so Spark users are no longer refused
items.done: ana reads a masked table in Spark and sees masked values. bob's row filter returns only his rows. Neither can reach the raw files
items.note: a Cairn-planned scan through Trino: cairn_spark.governed_read reads as the user, with their masks and row filters, partitioned; the catalog still refuses the files (tests/test_spark_e2e.py)

items.title: Spark on Kubernetes
items.summary: Cluster-mode submission and Spark Operator SparkApplications with no secret in the cluster (the driver signs in by workload identity), CairnSparkApplicationOperator for Airflow, driver RBAC and a history server in the chart; then per-team namespaces with quotas
items.done: An Airflow DAG submits a Spark job to the cluster as a pipeline user. Its lineage and run appear in Cairn, and the job is refused a table outside its grants
items.note: submission, operator, Airflow task and history server (tests/test_spark_k8s_e2e.py); on a full cluster in CI (kind): a cluster-mode job's driver pod signs in with its projected service-account token, starts an executor pod, reads a governed table and is refused another (tests/test_spark_kind_e2e.py); per-team quotas (tests/test_spark_teams_k8s.py)

items.title: Notebooks
items.summary: JupyterHub with Cairn sign-in; kernels with cairn-spark and Trino as the signed-in person; notebooks as catalog assets
items.done: A person signs in through Cairn, queries Trino and Spark from a notebook under their own policies, and the notebook appears in Cairn with lineage
items.note: JupyterHub signs people in through Cairn (OAuth client jupyterhub); each person's server gets a Cairn token of their own, suspended with them; %%sql on Trino and %cairn spark as the person; saved notebooks become catalog assets owned by them with lineage from their %%sql tables (cairn_lakehouse.jupyter, helm/jupyterhub/values-cairn.yaml, tests/test_jupyterhub_e2e.py with a real JupyterHub)

items.title: Streaming and CDC ingestion
items.summary: Kafka → Iceberg (Kafka Connect Iceberg sink) and Debezium CDC as governed pipelines, with exactly-once commits and schema evolution
items.done: A PostgreSQL table's changes arrive in an Iceberg table within a minute, with lineage from the source and quality monitors on freshness
items.note: Kafka JSON and Debezium CDC into Iceberg (cairn streams): upserts and deletes, offsets in the table snapshots for exactly once, rejects, schema evolution, source lineage (tests/test_streams_e2e.py)

items.title: Workload management and chargeback
items.summary: Trino resource groups and Spark quotas per team, with costs from Trino and Spark query statistics fed into the cost report automatically
items.done: Two teams' queries are isolated under load, and each team's compute and storage costs appear per day without manual posting
items.note: a resource group per team, tested under load on real Trino with Cairn deciding every action: team A's flood runs two at a time, queues four and is refused beyond, while team B's queries start at once (tests/test_workload_e2e.py); each team's compute (Trino queries with queued time, table compute, Spark runs) and storage (the lakehouse's tables sized daily from Cairn Catalog, CAIRN_COST_LAKEHOUSE_USD_PER_TB_MONTH, and warehouses) per day, by people's teams and tables' owners, without posting (GET /reports/costs/teams, same test); Spark compute is priced per application from its runs (CAIRN_COST_SPARK_USD_PER_CORE_HOUR); team warehouses scale to zero and their workers follow the load, with node-hours priced in the cost report (tests/test_warehouses_scaling_e2e.py); cost budgets per domain, owner, platform, tables, warehouse or AI, with threshold and forecast alerts once a period (tests/test_budgets.py); per-query Trino costs attributed to people, teams and tables (L60)

items.title: Machine learning
items.summary: MLflow tracking and model registry behind Cairn sign-in; models and features as catalog assets, with lineage from training tables
items.done: A model trained in Spark is registered as a pipeline user. Cairn shows its lineage to the training tables, and access to the model follows Cairn's policy
items.note: MLflow behind Cairn sign-in (/v1/ml): runs attributed to the caller, an owned and governed registry, versions in the catalog with lineage from training tables, serving through Cairn with USE_ML_MODEL (tests/test_ml_e2e.py, trained with scikit-learn); feature tables as catalog assets with their lineage, declared by the table's owners (tests/test_feature_tables.py); an online feature store: feature tables served by entity key, kept in step with the table's snapshots, each lookup governed as a read (masks as Trino applies them, row-filtered callers refused) (tests/test_online_features_e2e.py); model monitoring: every served call logged, drift (PSI) against the training table or a reference period, accuracy from labels, alerts on drift, payloads for the model's managers only (tests/test_ml_e2e.py, tests/test_model_monitoring_e2e.py); Spark training and model servers in the chart (templates/ml-workloads.yaml: cairn.mlflow.trainingJobs as CronJobs/Jobs running spark-submit in the Spark image, signed in by the service account's projected token with no Secret, env secrets refused, training pods taking no connections; cairn.mlflow.modelServers as Deployments of MLflow's model server wired into the API's CAIRN_ML_SERVING, reached only by the API's pods, MLflow admitting them), tested on kind (tests/test_ml_chart_kind.py, job spark-kind: the chart's Job trained with pyspark.ml and registered the model through Cairn as the bound user with table lineage, the chart's model server served it through Cairn, 403 without USE_ML_MODEL, another pod refused) and rendered with kubeconform (job helm). The kind test passes in CI (job spark-kind)

items.title: Open data sharing
items.summary: Iceberg REST sharing to external recipients, with recipient identities, expiry and revocation in Cairn
items.done: A recipient in another organisation reads a shared table with pyiceberg. Revoking the share stops access at once
items.note: shares through Iceberg REST: recipient credential, only the shared tables, read-only scoped keys, expiry, revocation at once, never a masked or filtered table (/v1/shares, Pipelines → Shares, tests/test_shares_e2e.py); the same shares through the open Delta Sharing protocol (/v1/delta-sharing: a profile file with the share's bearer token, the shared tables only, the current snapshot's Parquet files as pre-signed Cairn Store URLs signed with the catalog's scoped read-only keys, masked or filtered tables and tables with row-level deletes refused), tested with the real delta-sharing client reading a shared table and refused at once after revocation (tests/test_delta_sharing_e2e.py). Not yet: publishing to Snowflake (it needs a Snowflake account to test against); clean rooms: approved aggregate templates only, k-anonymous results, the room's own Trino identity reading only its tables (/v1/clean-rooms, tests/test_trino_e2e.py); differentially private rooms: Laplace noise on counts and clipped sums, an epsilon budget spent atomically and refused once used (tested on Trino); outside parties (partner:<name>) signing in with a secret shown once, uploading their data as a table only the room reads, proposing and running templates (tested on Trino with the real store and catalog)

items.title: Disaster recovery across regions
items.summary: Store replication, catalog and Cairn database replicas, and a tested failover runbook with measured recovery point and recovery time objectives
items.done: A region is lost in a test. The standby serves the lakehouse with the recorded RPO and RTO
items.note: standby store by bucket replication, standby PostgreSQL by streaming, a failover runbook and cairn dr reconcile (tables whose newest files never arrived move back to their newest whole commit); drill in CI with the primary region killed: RPO 4 of 10 commits (4.3 s), RTO about 2 s (tests/test_dr_drill.py); automatic failover (cairn dr watch): the standby databases promoted and DNS repointed by TSIG-signed RFC 2136 updates once the whole primary is lost and only onto a healthy standby, never failing back by itself; drilled with a real BIND server and Cairn's own database (audit chain whole, writes taken), DNS switched 1.4 s after the loss

items.title: Scale and assurance
items.summary: Load tests: PDP p99 under 5 ms cached at 2k rps, catalog decisions on 1k-table jobs, store throughput. Chaos tests. An external penetration test. KMS or HSM for gateway keys
items.done: Published results in CI, and pentest findings closed
items.note: in CI: cached decisions p99 0.02 ms at about 107k/s on one thread and a 1,000-table catalog decision in 0.6 s cold, 0.1 s warm (tests/test_scale_decisions.py, after indexing policies by privilege, compiling target patterns once and a cheaper cache key); chaos with a replica killed mid-commit, the database restarted and the store crashed, nothing acknowledged lost or doubled (catalog/conformance/test_chaos.py); every route refused to strangers but a reviewed public list, security headers (tests/test_route_security.py); KMS, Key Vault, Cloud KMS and KMIP HSMs for store keys (L22); the gateway's identity kept only wrapped by Vault transit or AWS KMS (CAIRN_GATEWAY_KEY_KMS, cairn gateway-keys wrap, Helm cairn.gateway.keys.kms), re-unwrapped every cache_seconds so a revoked token or disabled key stops it (503, no restart), tested with the real gateway process and an agent against Vault 1.20 and local-kms (tests/test_gateway_kms.py, job python); store throughput at 50,000 objects of 16 KiB and 256 of 8 MiB, every byte checked, published as the store-throughput artifact (job store; locally 3,000 small objects: 1,474 puts/s and 997 gets/s at concurrency 32). Still 🟡: the external penetration test needs a third party, and its findings closed; KMIP, Key Vault and Cloud KMS are not offered for the gateway's keys yet

items.title: Data residency
items.summary: Lakehouse namespaces pinned to a region
items.done: Regulated data stays in its region: stored there, processed only by deployments the pin allows, sent only to allowed regions; even an administrator cannot move it by a setting
items.note: Rules file shared by Cairn and Cairn Catalog (cairn.residency in the chart). The catalog keeps pinned tables in their region's location (create, register, commit, write.*.path, clone, rename, namespace location), refusing an administrator too. Trino and lakehouse engines read pinned tables only in an allowed CAIRN_REGION; shares and reverse syncs need an allowed destination region. Copies made by SQL follow the pin: a Trino statement reading a pinned table and writing outside the regions its pin allows (an unpinned namespace, another region, another catalog) is refused before it runs, an administrator's too (each statement's reads and writes followed by its query id, shared by Cairn's replicas); namespaces never inherit a pin. Cairn Store reads the same file: replication (and two-way sync), backups to sinks (on request, scheduled, continuous), write-back mounts and tier transitions go only to destinations whose residency_region the pin allows, checked when configured and for every object sent. Tested with the real store, catalog, Trino and Cairn, and a second store standing in for the other regions (tests/test_residency_e2e.py)

items.done: "Revenue per region from paid orders" becomes a checked, scheduled derived table; a broken one is fixed from its failed runs; nothing ships without the person's approval; the counterpart of Snowflake's CoCo
items.note: /v1/pipeline-agent/tasks (migration 0119): the model proposes a derived table and checks (never sees rows); each try is planned, previewed and checked on Trino as the person, writing nothing, failures fed back (3 tries); approval creates or updates the derived table as theirs, refreshes it and checks the result; the pipeline returned as a bundle resource. Tested on real Trino with a scripted model (tests/test_trino_e2e.py); 🟡 a live-model suite runs in CI job live-model when the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret is set (not yet run)

items.title: CoWork: scheduled tasks and an approved outbox
items.summary: The assistant works for a person on a schedule and sends to Slack or email only once they approve
items.done: "Every Monday, summarise last week's orders" runs as its owner and lands in their artifacts; sending it to #sales waits for their click, and data they may not export never leaves; the counterpart of Snowflake's CoWork
items.note: /ai/scheduled-tasks and /ai/outbox (migration 0120): cron at most hourly, research runs as the owner (read-only tools, their budget), notifications with Send/Don't send buttons, targets only from operator allow-lists, approval re-checks EXPORT_DATASET on every source and redacts PII, expiry, suspended owners paused. Tested with Mailpit, a Slack Web API stand-in and a scripted model (tests/test_cowork.py); 🟡 a live-model suite runs in CI job live-model when the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret is set (not yet run); Slack stays a stand-in there (there is no Slack workspace)

items.title: Connectors: SQL Server change data capture
items.summary: SQL Server tables mirrored into the lakehouse through CDC
items.done: The Microsoft operational databases arrive change by change without Debezium; the counterpart of Openflow's SQL Server connector
items.note: Mirrors accept mssql:// connections: CDC and a primary key checked (refused with the commands to run), a copy from the highest captured LSN (or the capture instance's start), whole transactions in commit order with old values for key changes, LSNs as offsets, purged changes reported. Tested with SQL Server 2022 and the real store and catalog (tests/test_mirror_mssql_e2e.py)

items.title: Connectors: MongoDB change streams
items.summary: MongoDB collections mirrored into the lakehouse
items.done: Document data arrives change by change, one row per document, new fields as new columns; the counterpart of Openflow's MongoDB connector
items.note: Mirrors accept mongodb:// connections (migration 0121 widens positions for resume tokens): replica set and collection checked, a copy from the cluster's operation time, inserts, updates (current document), replacements and deletes keyed by _id, transactions whole, resume tokens as positions, a dropped collection or lost oplog reported. Tested with MongoDB 7 and the real store and catalog (tests/test_mirror_mongo_e2e.py)

items.title: Document sources: SharePoint and Google Drive
items.summary: Folders kept in a store prefix and indexed by a files pipe
items.done: Contracts in SharePoint and notes in Drive become searchable text, AI fields and SQL rows under Cairn's policies; the counterpart of Openflow's SharePoint and Google Drive connectors
items.note: /v1/document-sources (migration 0122): Microsoft Graph (client credentials) and Drive (service account) listings with subfolders and pages, changed, moved and deleted files followed, Google Docs exported, size limit, keys from secret scopes as the owner. Tested with the real store, catalog and files pipe against a local stand-in for Graph and Drive (tests/test_doc_sources_e2e.py); not yet against a live tenant

items.title: AI gateway for agent code
items.summary: Anthropic- and OpenAI-compatible model endpoints in Cairn, called with Cairn tokens
items.done: Agents written in any framework call models through Cairn: no provider key in agent code, every call as a person or their agent, allowed models, budgets and rate limits, metered and audited; the counterpart of Databricks' Unity Gateway (part 1 of the Agent Bricks counterpart)
items.note: /v1/ai/gateway/anthropic/v1/messages, /v1/ai/gateway/openai/v1/chat/completions, /v1/ai/gateway/models: USE_AI_GATEWAY per model, the agent scope model, shared budgets and allowances, per-person rate limit, streaming passed through and metered. Tested with the official SDKs against a stand-in provider (tests/test_ai_gateway.py)

items.title: Code-first agents: cairn agents init, dev, deploy
items.summary: From an empty directory to a deployed agent app run as the person asking
items.done: A team writes an agent in plain Python, LangGraph or the OpenAI Agents SDK, tests it offline, runs it locally with their own Cairn token, and deploys it without wiring runtime, model keys, sessions or access by hand; the counterpart of Databricks' Agent Bricks CLI
items.note: cairn.agentkit (runtime, ctx with gateway-routed SDK clients and governed SQL, offline test kit, three templates), /v1/agent-apps (migration 0123): an agent identity per app, per-run tokens for the caller narrowed to the app's scopes and revoked after, sessions kept by Cairn, the process runtime and the Kubernetes runtime (a pod per app from the agent runtime image, reached only by Cairn, the chart's Role). Each invocation is an MLflow run in the app's experiment, under the caller's name, metrics only. Tested end to end (tests/test_agent_apps.py, tests/test_agent_apps_mlflow.py against a real MLflow, tests/test_agent_apps_k8s.py on kind)

items.title: Agent trace intelligence
items.summary: What each agent's tool calls and model use say: runs, errors, loops, slow calls, cost, and outliers against its own baseline
items.done: An operator sees which agent is stuck retrying, failing, slowing down or spending far more than it used to, before people complain or the budget runs out; owners see the same for their own agents
items.note: cairn.ai.trace_insights, /v1/agent-traces/insights (and per agent), /v1/agent-traces/settings (admin, audited); every traced tool call records its run (migration 0124): a custom agent's run, an agent app's run token, an OAuth session; key agents' calls are split into sessions. Findings with severity: loops, error rate, refusals, slow calls, flagged text, and volume, cost, latency, calls-per-run and error outliers against the agent's previous weeks. Tested end to end through the real services and HTTP API with real recorded MCP calls from a real agent key, a custom agent's real run and real usage metering (tests/test_agent_trace_insights.py)

items.title: Grounded answers with sources
items.summary: A question answered only from a vector index's passages, citing them
items.done: People ask the support articles or contracts a question and get an answer they can check: every sentence points to the rows it rests on, and Cairn says when the data does not answer it; the counterpart of retrieval-augmented answers in Databricks' and Snowflake's AI layers, under Cairn's policies
items.note: POST /v1/vectors/<name>/answer: passages retrieved as the caller (refused under masks and row filters), numbered and answered by the deployment's model through the metered, budgeted model path; citations actually used [{n, key, chunk, text, score}], sentences without a valid citation flagged, a refusal when no passage supports an answer, audited without content. Tested end to end on a real lakehouse table (tests/test_vectors_answer_e2e.py)

items.title: Serving tables (interactive analytics and hybrid tables)
items.summary: A lakehouse or derived table kept as a row store in PostgreSQL, looked up in milliseconds under the table's own policies
items.done: Applications and dashboards that need answers by key in milliseconds read the governed lakehouse table without a second, ungoverned copy; the counterpart of Snowflake hybrid tables and Databricks online tables
items.note: cairn.dataaccess.serving, /v1/serving (migration 0127): owners or operators declare a serving table (primary key, secondary indexes) over an Iceberg table; Cairn keeps it in a PostgreSQL database it manages, synced from the table's snapshots (only the added files on an append, a row-hash diff on rewrites, a full resync on a schema change), with the freshness lag reported. Reads by key, key range and simple filters (GET .../rows, POST .../lookup) go through the data preview's decisions: read access, aggregation/projection policies, row filters applied in PostgreSQL, Trino's column masks, a masked column never compared, fail closed. Writable (hybrid) tables take owners' writes, readable at once and upserted into the Iceberg table on the next sync. Tested end to end with Trino, Cairn Store and Catalog and PostgreSQL (tests/test_serving_tables_e2e.py: masked and row-filtered answers equal Trino's; p50 about 9-13 ms, p95 about 17-47 ms per key lookup through the API on a shared 4-CPU runner). Not done: a Trino catalog over the serving tables

items.title: Streaming transformations
items.summary: A SQL SELECT applied to each micro-batch of a stream before it lands
items.done: Cleaned, cast and filtered data arrives within seconds of being sent, without waiting for a derived table's schedule; the counterpart of transformations in Snowflake's Snowpipe Streaming and Databricks' streaming tables
items.note: transform on json and http streams: one row-for-row SELECT over batch, checked when the stream is defined (no joins or other tables, key kept, binds in the engine), run in-process in a sandboxed DuckDB (no files, network or extensions); failing rows go to the stream's rejects, filtered rows are skipped and the offsets still move on, a new table takes the transform's types (migration 0126). Tested end to end through an HTTP ingest stream into a real lakehouse table read through Trino (tests/test_stream_transform_e2e.py)

items.title: External Iceberg catalogs, governed
items.summary: Another organisation's or a cloud Iceberg REST catalog queried in Trino as a catalog of its own
items.done: Partner and cloud tables are queried in place under the same grants, masks and row filters as the lakehouse, read-only by default, with their credential never leaving Cairn; the counterpart of Unity Catalog's and Snowflake's catalog federation
items.note: /v1/external-catalogs (migration 0125): registration with a credential reference (secret scope or CAIRN_EXTCAT_*), Trino's dynamic catalogs (CREATE CATALOG by cairn-catalogs only) signing in through Cairn's OAuth token broker with Trino's own key, namespaces, tables and schemas catalogued, read-only enforcement, re-added after a Trino restart. Tested with a second real Cairn Catalog and Store on Trino 484: masked, filtered and refused users, writes refused (tests/test_external_catalogs_e2e.py)

items.title: Share observability
items.summary: Who reads what through each lakehouse share
items.done: Share owners see each recipient's requests, tables read, loads, refusals and failures, find unused and expiring shares and recipients reading tables with failing quality, and are told before a share ends; the counterpart of Delta Sharing's and Snowflake's share usage views
items.note: Per share, day and table counts from Cairn Catalog's per-request questions and the token endpoint, with retention (migration 0125); GET /v1/shares/<name>/usage, GET /v1/shares/usage/overview joined with the quality status; share.expiring and share.unused notices once each. Tested with pyiceberg as the recipient against the real store and catalog (tests/test_share_usage_e2e.py); refusals outside a share's namespaces are decided by the catalog alone and count as requests

items.title: Agents and skills in the marketplace
items.summary: Agent apps, custom agents and extensions listed and requested beside data products
items.done: People find agents and reusable skills where they find data, ask for them with a purpose and duration, and get exactly the right to use them until it expires; the counterpart of Databricks' and Snowflake's marketplace listings of agents and apps
items.note: /marketplace/listings and /marketplace/search (migration 0125): listings by the agent's or skill's owner, searched with data products, requests in the marketplace's queue, approval granting a time-boxed persona with USE_AGENT on urn:li:cairnAgent:<name> (USE_SKILL on urn:li:cairnSkill:<name>) only, revoked by the sweep at expiry and on delisting. Tested through the HTTP API with a real agent app process (tests/test_marketplace_agents.py)

items.title: Agent automations from the CLI: cairn tasks
items.summary: CoWork scheduled tasks and their outbox from a terminal or a script
items.done: Someone who lives in the terminal (or a CI job acting for a person) sets up recurring research, runs it now, reads the report and approves or rejects what goes out, without the web UI
items.note: cairn.agentkit.tasks: list, create (name, prompt, cron, max steps, Slack or email), show (last runs), output (a run's report), run, pause/resume, delete, outbox, approve/reject, --json; CAIRN_URL and CAIRN_TOKEN/CAIRN_TOKEN_FILE from the environment only; agent credentials refused. Tested by running the real CLI in a subprocess against a real Cairn API server, with the report sent to a Slack stand-in only after approval (tests/test_tasks_cli.py)

items.title: Intent-based security for agents
items.summary: Each agent run declares its purpose and the kinds of action it allows; anything else is refused
items.done: An agent asked to summarise revenue cannot, even through a prompt injection or a bug, write, share, export or read tables the task does not concern, though its scopes would allow it; operators can require every agent run to say what it is for
items.note: cairn.identity.intents: intents (purpose, actions read, query, propose, write, share, export, model, admin, tables, domains) on run tokens (agent app invocations), custom agent definitions (migration 0124) and key agents; every agent request classified (HTTP by route, SQL by statement kind, tools by tool) and refused outside its intent (403, audited agent.intent_denied); /v1/agent-intents/settings (require intents, fail closed), /denials, /classify. Tested end to end through the HTTP API with real agent keys, run tokens, a real SQLite warehouse, a custom agent run and a real agent app process whose model call is refused (tests/test_agent_intents.py, tests/test_agent_apps.py)

items.title: SCD type 2 and medallion layers
items.summary: Derived tables that keep every version of a row, and bronze, silver and gold on the tables Cairn writes
items.done: Dimension history (what a customer's tier was last quarter) without hand-written MERGE logic, and a gold layer that means something: owned, described and passing its contract; the counterpart of Databricks' APPLY CHANGES (SCD type 2) and medallion architecture
items.note: Derived mode scd2 (key, tracked): one Trino MERGE per refresh closes changed and removed keys (valid_to, is_current), inserts new versions, writes untracked changes in place, changes nothing when nothing changed; a full rebuild is refused once there is history. layer on pipes, streams and derived tables and /v1/medallion: kept (migration 0126), tagged in the catalog, gold refused without an owner, a description and a met contract or passing monitors, and re-checked in the listing. Tested end to end on Trino with the real store and catalog (tests/test_scd2_medallion_e2e.py)

items.title: Agent memory
items.summary: Governed long-term memory for agents, about the people they work for
items.done: An agent remembers a person's preferences and context across sessions without ever recalling one person's memories for another, holding values masking protects or credentials, or keeping anything the person cannot see and delete
items.note: cairn.ai.agent_memory (migration 0129): memories per agent and person (written by the agent through its run token, scope memory, ctx.memory.remember/recall/forget, or by the person), team and shared memories written only by people; recall by meaning (the search-by-meaning embedder) plus recency; the source run recorded; PII (the classifier's value detectors), credentials and instructions refused; size cap with eviction, retention and purge; GET/DELETE /v1/me/agent-memories under the person's own identity; audited without content. Tested end to end with a real agent app process remembering in one session and recalling in another, as one person and not as another (tests/test_agent_memory.py)

items.title: AI search and document parsing in SQL and pipelines
items.summary: ai_search(index, query, k) in Trino SQL over a vector index; tables and charts extracted from PDFs and images as data
items.done: An analyst retrieves passages and joins them to their rows in one query, under the same policies as the API's search; a report's tables and its charts' numbers land as JSON next to its text; the counterpart of Databricks' vector_search() and ai_parse_document, and Snowflake's Cortex Search and document AI
items.note: Cairn's Trino functions plugin (plugins/java/cairn-trino-functions, built inside the Trino image, installed by Helm cairn.trino.functions): ai_search returns array(row(key, chunk, text, score)) searched by Cairn as the query's user (read access, no mask or row filter on the source; Cairn's own identities refused), metered under the person with a daily cap. cairn.pipelines.parse: tables from PDFs' text layer without a model; pages that draw graphics rendered (PDFium, in a child process) and read by the deployment's multimodal model for chart series and pictured tables; POST /v1/documents/parse (kept per person, migration 0128) and files pipes' "ai": {"parse": true}. Tested end to end: a real Trino calling ai_search on a real index in the store and catalog (tests/test_ai_search_e2e.py); a generated PDF with a table and a drawn chart, the model behind the provider stand-in, the deterministic path without a model, the API and a files pipe (tests/test_document_parse_e2e.py)

items.title: Dynamic model routing in the AI gateway
items.summary: Virtual model names (cairn-auto, operators' routes) that map to ordered models with rules and fallback
items.done: Agent code asks for cairn-auto and gets an answer when a provider is down, slow or rate-limited, from the cheapest model that fits the request and that the caller may use, metered on the model that answered
items.note: cairn.ai.gateway_routes (migration 0129): candidates with capabilities (tools, vision), input size and timeouts; the route's cost ceiling, strategy (ordered, cheapest) and latency budget; fallback on 5xx, timeouts, unreachable providers and 429 (streams before the first byte); candidates the caller may not use skipped, none left refused; named upstreams (CAIRN_AI_GATEWAY_UPSTREAMS, …_MODEL_UPSTREAMS); X-Cairn-Model/X-Cairn-Route; operator API /v1/ai/gateway/routes (MANAGE_SYSTEM_OPERATIONS), audited (gateway.route_saved, gateway.routed). Tested through the HTTP gateway with the Anthropic SDK and two provider stand-ins, the first failing or rate-limiting and the second answering, plus cost, capability, size and latency routes (tests/test_ai_gateway_routes.py)

items.title: Agentic abuse detection
items.summary: Prompt injection and data exfiltration through agents detected, blocked and counted
items.done: Instructions planted in a ticket, a description or a monitor name cannot steer an agent into leaking data, and an agent that keeps trying is paused before it does damage
items.note: cairn.ai.abuse (migration 0129): rule-based detectors with severities on inputs reaching models (gateway messages, custom agents' tool results, MCP results) for injection, and on outputs and tool arguments (gateway answers, streams included; custom agents' answers and tool calls; MCP arguments) for secrets, PII dumps (the classifier's value detectors), destinations outside an allowlist and tools out of scope; an optional model judge; blocking at a severity; per-agent counters in the agent insights and auto-pause after N critical findings; /v1/agent-abuse/findings, /settings, /scan; audited. Tested end to end through the gateway (an agent key, a provider stand-in) and a custom agent, with planted injection in tool results and attempted exfiltration: blocked, recorded, the agents paused (tests/test_agent_abuse.py)

items.title: Zero-copy Parquet
items.summary: Parquet files already in the store registered as an Iceberg table in place, with new files added as they land
items.done: A data set exported by another system becomes a governed, queryable table without a copy or a load job, and stays in step as files arrive; the counterpart of Snowflake's external tables and Databricks' CONVERT TO DELTA / Iceberg's add_files
items.note: POST /v1/lakehouse/parquet-tables (MANAGE_INGESTION): files only from CAIRN_PARQUET_BUCKETS, read access checked (READ_FILES on the path, or a volume grant), schema inferred from the footers and checked across files, identity partitions from Hive-style paths, the files added by reference (statistics from footers, a name mapping, gc.enabled=false), lineage from the store prefix, and refresh/every_minutes adding new files as the registering person (migration 0128). Tested end to end on the real store, catalog and Trino (tests/test_parquet_tables_e2e.py): queried as a masked user, partitions from paths, new files added incrementally, and the manifests referencing the same object keys (nothing copied)

items.title: Sandboxes for agent code
items.summary: Python (and SQL over DuckDB) that agents and people run, a container per run, data only through the person's governed token
items.done: Agents can compute, transform files and make charts without Cairn trusting their code: it cannot reach the network, other runs or Cairn's credentials, and what it reads through Cairn is masked and filtered for the person it works for
items.note: cairn.ai.sandboxes: POST /v1/sandboxes/runs (also the run_python tool for custom agents, the assistant and MCP, and ctx.run_python in agent apps); docker (a container per run, --network none, uid 1000, read-only root, CPU, memory, process and time limits, in-memory working directory) or a Kubernetes pod per run (NetworkPolicy denying all traffic, optional runtime class); network only through a per-run egress proxy (operator-allowed hosts, private addresses refused, Cairn as http://cairn); a run token for the person through the sandbox's agent identity, narrowed to read and query_data and revoked at the end; RUN_CODE, per-person and global concurrency caps, runs recorded and metered (migration 0130, /v1/sandboxes/usage) and audited. Tested end to end with real containers: a result and a generated file, network refused, time and memory limits enforced, a governed query from inside the sandbox seeing a masked column masked (tests/test_sandboxes_e2e.py)

items.title: AI data packages and agents on shared data
items.summary: A share with its semantic context, signed, and the provider's agents answering the recipient over the shared tables only
items.done: A partner's agents understand what they were given (descriptions, columns, glossary, governed metrics, sample questions) and can trust it came from the provider; the provider can offer its own agent on the data without opening anything else
items.note: cairn.dataaccess.share_packages: PUT /v1/shares/<share>/package publishes a versioned manifest (tables, columns, glossary, metrics over shared tables only, sample questions, attached agents) signed as a JWS with Cairn's published key; the recipient fetches it with the share's credential (/v1/shares/recipient/package). Agent apps attached to a share (/v1/shares/<share>/agents) are invoked by the recipient as identity type share-recipient: run token narrowed to model (model use decided for the provider, metered to the recipient), data only through a lakehouse token for the share (ctx.catalog()); runs recorded per recipient and audited (migration 0130). Tested end to end with the real store and catalog, a real agent process and the gateway's model stand-in: signature verified, shared table read, other tables refused, revocation stopping both (tests/test_share_packages_e2e.py)

items.title: Cairn in Excel and Google Sheets
items.summary: An Office add-in and a Google Sheets add-on with QUERY, METRIC and ASK functions and a pane to sign in, browse governed metrics and insert them
items.done: Analysts get governed numbers in the spreadsheet they already use, as themselves: masked, filtered and permitted as in Cairn, with the metric meaning what it means everywhere else; the counterpart of Snowflake's and Databricks' Excel and Sheets connectors
items.note: cairn/addins: the Excel add-in (manifest, shared runtime, custom functions CAIRN.QUERY/METRIC/ASK, task pane) and the Apps Script add-on (CAIRN_QUERY/METRIC/ASK, sidebar, hourly refresh trigger), built per Cairn by build.mjs. Both are OAuth public clients configured by the operator (CAIRN_EXCEL_ADDIN_ORIGINS, CAIRN_SHEETS_ADDON_SCRIPT_IDS): authorization code with PKCE, the person's tokens scoped read, query_data, model, short-lived and rotating; CORS for the Office origin only; /data/sheets/{query,metric,ask,metrics} answer 2-D grids. Tested end to end against a real Cairn API server (tests/test_spreadsheet_addins.py): the add-ins' own JavaScript in Node signs in through the real consent page, a masked column comes back masked, the row filter holds, a denied table is refused, refresh rotates once for concurrent calls, sign-out revokes. Not tested end to end: running inside Excel and Sheets themselves (host APIs are stand-ins; the task pane and sidebar UI are not exercised), and the manifest against Microsoft's XSD (checked structurally)

items.title: Profiles, mobile app and desktop
items.summary: A per-person profile the assistant and scheduled tasks use; the workspace as an installable app with push notifications; a desktop app
items.done: The assistant knows who it works for (role, team, persona, language, pins, standing instructions) without being told each time; people use Cairn on their phone and desktop like an app, and hear about what concerns them
items.note: cairn.identity.profiles (migration 0131): GET/PUT /v1/me/profile (role, team, default persona among the person's, language, pins filtered by what they may see, notification channels as the hub's settings, standing instructions), people only (agents never reach /v1/me), given to the assistant's chat and CoWork's research as data after the rules; a Profile page under Platform. The PWA at /cairn-ui/app.html: manifest, icons, a service worker caching the app shell only (never API responses), an offline page; web push as empty VAPID-signed messages to allow-listed push services with the operator's key from a file. cairn/desktop: an Electron app, superseded by Cairn Desktop 1.0 (L131). Tested end to end: the profile API over HTTP with a chat and a CoWork task seeing it, push against a stand-in push service verifying the VAPID JWT (tests/test_profiles.py); Chromium on the built UI against a real Cairn: manifest, service worker, shell-only cache, offline page, the Profile page round-trip, phone-width layouts and axe (tests/test_pwa_e2e.py); the desktop app: see L131. Not tested end to end: a browser's subscription with a real vendor push service

items.title: Talk to your app
items.summary: A chat panel for data apps: questions about what the app shows, answered with the app's declared context and the asker's own access
items.done: People get answers about the numbers in front of them without leaving the app, and never see more through the chat than the app itself would show them
items.note: cairn.dataaccess.app_chat: chat on a data app (description, tables, queries, a context endpoint; migration 0130); POST /v1/apps/<name>/chat (USE_APP) runs the declared queries as the asker (masks, row filters, refusals), describes only tables they may see, asks the running app's context endpoint as them (never with Cairn's or the app's credentials), and calls the model through the AI gateway as them; answers cite the tables used; audited without content. Ask about this app on the Data apps tab. Tested end to end with a real app process, a real warehouse and the gateway's model stand-in: the asker's masking held in the answer (tests/test_app_chat_e2e.py)

items.title: Cairn Ontology
items.summary: An ontology compiled from the catalog and the query log: business terms, relationships, metrics and bridge tables, reviewed as proposals and used to ground and check generated SQL (a Rust port of the compiler at the heart of NVIDIA's open-source Auto Ontology, Apache-2.0)
items.done: Agents and people ask in business words and get SQL that joins the way the data is really joined; a wrong join is flagged before anyone trusts its number; nobody sees ontology elements over data they may not see
items.note: cairn/ontology (cairn-ontology, Rust; PostgreSQL or SQLite): catalog snapshots diffed incrementally with allow/deny table filters, the query log parsed with sqlparser (tables, columns, joins, unions, aggregations) and merged by shape with usage counts; the semantic pipeline ported (column profiling with date-notation inference, FK and junction detection, column descriptions, terms with display names and synonyms, semantic FK resolution with pruning and join defaults, metrics from the query log, bridge-table join patterns, embeddings) with tables processed in parallel and committed in canonical order, cancellation, resumable and incremental versioned runs; model calls through Cairn's AI gateway (OpenAI chat with structured outputs and embeddings, added to the gateway) as the compiler's agent identity; /validate-sql (unknown join paths, joins contradicting keys, fan-out, deprecated columns, definition mismatches), search by name and meaning, JSON, JSON-LD and Turtle exports, provenance. In Cairn (cairn.context.ontology_compiler, /v1/ontology): sync on a schedule and on demand (MANAGE_GLOSSARIES), results as context-inbox proposals (accepted terms become glossary terms linked to their columns, joins and metrics approved definitions), reads filtered by catalog visibility, Ask-your-data grounded in the relationships and its SQL checked (fail-open with a warning), MCP tools ontology_search_terms, ontology_relationships, ontology_validate_sql; Helm, Compose, image; an Ontology area in the Semantic models hub with a graph view. Tested end to end with the real compiler on PostgreSQL, a real Cairn, Cairn Store, Cairn Catalog and Trino (queries run through Trino are the query log) and the provider stand-in behind the gateway (tests/test_ontology_e2e.py); 42 Rust unit tests carrying the upstream tests' intent

items.title: Cairn Flows
items.summary: One orchestration model: a flow is a DAG mixing any step (SQL, derived tables, checks, pipes, streams, notebooks, Python, Spark, dbt, agents, Airflow DAGs, approvals, waits, branches, for-each, notifications), triggered by cron, table changes, other flows, people and agents, run as its owner
items.done: People and agents orchestrate everything the platform does in one place, as the owner and under their grants, from a canvas, from YAML in git or through MCP; nothing runs as anyone else, and a run starts once however many replicas tick
items.note: cairn.flows (migration 0132): one definition (kind: flow, YAML or JSON, with layout for the canvas) checked with precise paths (cycles, unknown references and step types, templates over steps that do not come before, branch sides); safe {{ }} expressions over parameters and earlier outputs (AST-walked, never evaluated); typed parameters with defaults; triggers on cron with a time zone, dataset changes (the change feed: Trino's commits, pipes, streams, dbt, derived tables, flows), after another flow, manual and API; drafts and published versions (runs pin one; diffs); owners, editors, viewers and admins; every step as the owner, failing closed; retries with backoff, time limits, cancel, rerun from a step, backfill over dates, skip/queue/allow concurrency, SLA alerts, notifications, OpenLineage lineage, audit; runs driven under a database lease and parked while they wait, so replicas share them and each start is claimed once. /v1/flows, a flows registry kind (bundles: plan, apply, drift, prune; Terraform cairn_flow), cairn flows list/validate/deploy/run/logs, MCP list_flows, run_flow, get_flow_run; SQL workflows run their steps through the same executors and open as flows. Tested: the engine, API, bundles and MCP on a real warehouse, with two engines on one database (tests/test_flows.py), and end to end on Trino, Cairn Catalog, Cairn Store and Docker: a derived table refreshed as the owner, a check stopping a report and telling the owner, a branch on a row count, a Trino write starting a flow, a Python step in a job container reading Trino with the owner's token, an approval over HTTP, and a refusal by Trino (tests/test_flows_e2e.py). The engine steps on the real engines (pipelines job): a stream step on a real Kafka broker parked until the stream's worker has written the topic's offsets into its table, then the flow going on and reading the rows on Trino, failing on its time limit and with Kafka unreachable (tests/test_flows_engines_e2e.py); a dbt step in a project image on cairn/dbt building a seed and a model on Trino as the owner, and as an owner without the grant refused by Trino with dbt's report in the step's log (same file; fixed on the way: dbt could not write its logs as the job's user, a commented profile: line broke the profile, Trino's certificate was not verified without a CA file); an airflow step starting a DAG in a real Airflow 3.3, waiting and going on, failing with a failed DAG run or an unknown DAG (tests/test_flows_airflow_e2e.py); a spark step in an image on cairn/spark building an Iceberg table through Cairn Catalog with a lakehouse session issued to the owner, refused for someone who may not see the schema, failing without a session or image (tests/test_flows_spark_e2e.py; Spark steps now run as the image's own user, CAIRN_FLOWS_SPARK_UID, and jobs use python3 where an image has no python). items.title: Airflow both ways
items.summary: A flow exported as an Airflow DAG; Airflow as a flow's runner; Airflow's DAGs shown in Cairn and converted to flows
items.done: Teams that run Airflow keep it: flows move to Airflow as reviewable DAG files with no secrets, Airflow can carry out a flow while every step still runs as its owner and the run history stays in Cairn, and existing DAGs become visible (to the people they belong to) and convertible
items.note: cairn.flows.airflow_dag: GET /v1/flows/{name}/airflow, cairn flows export-airflow (also from a file, without Cairn): order, trigger rules, retries, back-off, time limits, typed params, schedules in their time zone, table triggers (assets watched in the change feed) and max_active map; SQL, checks (new CairnCheckOperator), dbt, Spark and DAG triggers run natively as the connection's user; everything else (approvals, for-each, derived tables, agents, steps whose output others read) is delegated to Cairn as the owner through the new CairnFlowStepOperator, and branches through CairnFlowBranchOperator, each with a comment; what does not map is said in the file. runner: airflow: publishing writes cairn__<flow>.py into Airflow's DAG folder (CAIRN_FLOWS_AIRFLOW_DAGS: a mounted path, or a git folder's branch); Cairn starts runs over Airflow's REST API, follows the DAG run and its task instances into the run history, and each task runs its step in Cairn as the owner under a lease (POST /v1/flows/runs/{run}/steps/{step}/execute). GET /v1/airflow/dags and /{id} through Cairn's service account, shown only to the people a DAG belongs to (owners, team:/group: tags, their flows; fail closed), with tasks, runs and live states; the Airflow tab on the Flows page draws them read-only on the canvas; Convert to Cairn flow (POST .../convert) makes a draft when every task is a provider operator with literal arguments, else names each blocking task. Tested: golden files, the deploy targets (a directory and a real git repository), and with a real Airflow 3.3 (tests/test_flows_airflow_e2e.py, pipelines job): an export loaded by DagBag and the DAG processor with no errors, a runner-airflow flow run by Airflow with its branch skipped and an airflow step starting another DAG, Cairn's run history per step, the visibility rule, a conversion and a refusal; vitest for the Airflow tab. An exported DAG run by Airflow alone: its native SQL and check on Trino as the connection's user, a native dbt build (with the cairn/airflow image), a TriggerDagRunOperator starting and waiting for another DAG and a delegated step run in Cairn as the owner, the table in Trino and every task's status in Cairn's run history, and a failing check skipping what follows. The git-folder target with the real git-sync v4.8.0 image: publishing committed the DAG to a real repository served over HTTP, git-sync synced it into Airflow's folder, Airflow loaded and ran it from Cairn, and deleting the flow removed it (fixed: a deleted flow's DAG was never removed, its version being read after it was deleted). Airflow 2.10 as a runner over /api/v1 (tests/test_flows_airflow2_e2e.py): Basic sign-in, the deployed DAG importing on Airflow 2 (DAG/Param fall back to Airflow 2's modules), branch, wait and DAG trigger, each step run in Cairn as the owner, the DAGs listed with runs ordered by execution_date, a conversion reading the source by file token (fixed: Airflow 2's details leave owners empty, its source is plain text unless JSON is asked for, its schedule is schedule_interval), and wrong credentials refused. Left: an exported DAG's Spark task (CairnSparkApplicationOperator) run to completion: it needs the Spark Operator on a cluster (its SparkApplication is checked against a real API server and the operator's CRD in tests/test_spark_k8s_e2e.py)

items.title: Agents do infrastructure as code
items.summary: Agents plan and propose changes to Cairn's resources as code; people with the right privileges approve and apply them; Ask an agent drafts them from plain words
items.done: An agent can build what a team asks (a saved query, a nightly flow) as reviewable code, but nothing changes until a person who could make the change approves it, applies it as themselves and sees exactly what it does; secrets never pass through it
items.note: cairn.iac.changes (migration 0133): /v1/iac/changes (plan, propose, list, get, approve, reject, apply, commit, withdraw) and MCP iac_schema, iac_inventory, iac_export, iac_plan, iac_propose, iac_changes, iac_apply, iac_open_pr. A change is bundle YAML or Terraform files (cairn.iac.hcl reads the exported subset), with delete/allow_delete; the bundle engine plans it through Cairn's API in-process (an agent's plan reads as the person it acts for, read-only) with each field before and after. Agents need the new scope iac:propose; secrets are ${NAME} references, never values, and anything credential-like is refused; deletes and replaces need allow_delete. Approval needs APPROVE_IAC_CHANGE on every type touched (urn:li:iacKind:<type>) and a re-plan as the approver that comes out the same; the sponsor cannot approve (CAIRN_IAC_SELF_APPROVE allows it); agents never approve or apply. Applying is the approver's, as themselves, with variables used once; a plan that changed since approval is refused and goes back for approval. Commits to a branch of a git folder for review. Every step audited, approvers told (CAIRN_IAC_CHANGE_APPROVERS). UI: Changes under Settings, Infrastructure as code (readable per-resource diffs, approve/reject with a comment, apply, history, YAML and Terraform) with Ask an agent (CAIRN_IAC_AGENT_MODEL through the AI gateway, as the person; a proposed flow opens read-only on the canvas). Tested end to end (tests/test_iac_agent_e2e.py, python job): a real API and its MCP server over streamable HTTP with agent keys, a real git repository and the AI gateway to a stand-in provider answering with tool calls: plan with no side effects, propose, refused approvers (no privilege, the sponsor), approval and apply as the approver, drift refused and re-proposed, delete without allow_delete, secret values and credentials refused, scopes, a Terraform change, a git commit, Ask an agent drafting a flow, the audit log; vitest for the Changes view. Not tested: a pull request on a hosted git provider; for Ask an agent, a live-model suite runs in CI job live-model when the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret is set (not yet run)

items.title: Guided experience

items.done: Every kind of person finds their way: a new analyst, engineer, steward or admin is asked their role once and shown the first things to do, jumps anywhere by typing, reads the right docs beside their work, and never sees areas they can't use, while the API still decides every request
items.note: Onboarding: a role question on first visit to the home page (suggested from the profile's role; "Not now" is an answer), a checklist per role (analyst 5, engineer 4, steward 4, admin 5, explorer 4 steps), each linking to where it is done, ticked from the API as the person (saved queries, dashboards, SQL history, flows and their schedules, quality monitors, decided ontology proposals and access requests, AI gateway routes, budgets), by a visit or an in-app event, or by hand; kept in the profile (ui, migration 0134) so it follows the person; PUT /v1/ui/settings (MANAGE_GLOBAL_SETTINGS, Settings → Guided start) turns it off for everyone.
