items.title: CLI 2.0
items.summary: cairn for people: sign in with the browser, then query, search, show and ask as yourself; profiles for several Cairns; completion; one binary per platform
items.done: People and CI reach governed data from a terminal with the same access, masks and refusals as in the web app, without handling long-lived secrets, and install it without Python
items.note: cairn login: OAuth 2.0 device flow (RFC 8628) in cairn.identity.device (POST /oauth/device_authorization, the device-code grant on /oauth/token with authorization_pending, slow_down, expired_token, access_denied; no migration: the agents' token table); approval on the web UI's /device page with the person's browser session (passkey step-up optional); one-hour access tokens and rotating refresh tokens acting as the person (via cli), reuse signs the device out, suspended or SCIM-deactivated people lose them; Signed-in devices on the profile page and /admin/devices; tokens in the OS keychain (keyring) or a refused-unless-0600 file, never printed; --token-stdin; CAIRN_URL/CAIRN_TOKEN win. Profiles in ~/.config/cairn/config.toml (--profile, CAIRN_PROFILE, profiles list/use/remove), whoami. cairn query (/v1/statements: the SQL workspace's checks, then Trino as the person page by page, sealed cursors, Ctrl-C cancels in Trino; table, csv, json, jsonl, parquet; --limit, --warehouse), search, show (/v1/assets), ask; flows, iac plan/apply/validate/export and ontology status/compile through the profile; --output json, --quiet, --no-color, documented exit codes (0-5, 130), 403s naming the privilege, "did you mean"; completion for bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell (profiles and flows dynamic). Light cairn-cli wheel (cli/, no server dependencies), PyInstaller binaries (cli/cairn.spec, 21 MB on Linux), release workflow cairn-cli-release.yml (matrix, smoke tests, SHA256SUMS, Homebrew formula, signing behind absent secrets), deploy/cli/install.sh, deploy/homebrew/cairn.rb. Tested end to end (tests/test_cli_e2e.py, trino job, with the Python package and the Linux x86_64 binary): device sign-in through the API and in headless Chromium on /device, keyring and 0600 file, profiles and precedence, every format streamed over many pages as the person (masks, row filters), Ctrl-C cancelling in Trino, exit 4 on a refused table, warehouses, search, show, ask with a stand-in model provider, flows/iac/ontology, refresh rotation and reuse, logout and revocation from the profile page; plus the device flow on a real database, the client-only wheel in a clean venv, the install script against an HTTPS mirror, vitest for the pages. Also tested: cairn ontology status and compile --wait (source and binary) against Cairn with the real compiler on PostgreSQL, a person without MANAGE_GLOSSARIES refused with exit 4 (tests/test_ontology_e2e.py, trino job; it found the compiler's readiness check, SELECT 1, panicking its database thread on PostgreSQL, now fixed); the Linux binary keeping its sign-in in the Secret Service of an unlocked GNOME Keyring, found with secret-tool and removed on logout (cli/ci/keychain-smoke.sh; whoami --output json names the keyring backend in credential_backend). The release workflow runs on every push to the CLI: all five builds (Linux x86_64 and arm64, macOS arm64 and x86_64, Windows x86_64) built and smoke-tested on GitHub's runners (run 42576947234); each now also signs in through the platform's real keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, the Secret Service), and the macOS builds install the formula from a local tap (cli/ci/homebrew-smoke.sh: brew tap-new, brew install, brew test, completions, brew uninstall). Not yet: those keychain and Homebrew steps on macOS and Windows have yet to pass on GitHub's runners (they run only there), a published tap (brew tap <owner>/cairn from GitHub), and signing and notarization (no Apple Developer ID or Windows certificate yet)

items.title: Cairn Desktop 1.0
items.summary: Several workspaces in one app, the command line signed in with one click, native notifications, links and tray, dashboards readable offline, installers and updates
items.done: People use Cairn as an app on their computer, switch between their organisation's Cairns, get their terminal signed in without copying codes, hear about what concerns them, and still read the dashboards they opened when the network is gone; IT controls updates and caching
items.note: cairn/desktop (Electron 45.2.3, electron-builder 26.18.0, electron-updater 6.8.11): workspaces are the CLI's profiles (config.toml read and written byte for byte as the CLI does), each in its own session partition, a top bar and native menus to switch (Ctrl/Cmd+1…9), added by URL after /health answers as Cairn (https; http to localhost); sign-in is the web UI's own (SSO redirects followed, then back to the workspace's origin only); "Sign in the command line too" runs the bundled cairn login and approves its code with the session after checking the device is its own (the CLI keeps the tokens in the OS keychain; fallback: the /device page); inbox and page notifications as OS notifications opening the right page; cairn://<workspace>/<page> checked (unknown workspaces prompt to add); tray with unread count, switcher and Ask Cairn…; optional global shortcut; remembered window; spellcheck, zoom; dropped files go to pages that take them, else "Drop not supported here"; offline page with retry and the last viewed dashboards and reports as read-only snapshots (no scripts, sandboxed frame), per workspace, encrypted with safeStorage (nothing kept without a real keychain), limited and expiring, cleared on sign-out; "Install command line tool" (symlink or ~/.local/bin, user PATH on Windows); sandbox, context isolation, strict preloads, navigation allowlist, permission handler (camera and microphone asked), fuses (RunAsNode, NODE_OPTIONS, inspect off; cookie encryption, ASAR integrity, ASAR only), CSP on local pages; electron-updater from the rolling desktop-latest release or a generic feed, notify-only on unsigned macOS, off/notify/pin by the person, workspace settings or the computer's policy file. Server: GET /v1/desktop/policy, GET/PUT /admin/desktop/policy (cairn.identity.desktop; offline_cache, limits, updates, pinned_version, update_feed_url, sign_in_origins; audited; no migration). Release workflow cairn-desktop-release.yml (macOS arm64 and x64, Windows, Linux; CLI built first; smoke tests; SHA256SUMS; merged latest*.yml; signing and notarization behind absent secrets; hardened-runtime entitlements). Tested: the real app under xvfb with GNOME Keyring against two real Cairns and the CLI's PyInstaller binary (tests/test_desktop_e2e.py: add, sign in, two sessions, deep links, notifications, external links, CLI sign-in to cairn whoami, offline dashboard encrypted and read, cleared on sign-out, an administrator turning caching off, window state); the settings API (tests/test_desktop_policy.py); node unit tests for config sharing (against the CLI's own reader and writer), deep links, the allowlist, permissions, the cache, update policy, tray, menus, window state and the CLI helpers; a Linux unpacked build and AppImage smoke-tested (window and deep link, the CLI inside), and an AppImage updating itself from a local feed and holding at a pinned version. Also tested: the .deb built by electron-builder, installed with apt, run from /opt under xvfb in a D-Bus session with GNOME Keyring (safeStorage on gnome-libsecret with a round trip, the page's notification handed to the OS, a deep link, the CLI inside), then removed; the packaged app's self-test report (CAIRN_DESKTOP_SELF_TEST: tray, notifications reaching the main process, safeStorage) read by test/electron.smoke.test.js, since its fuses keep debuggers out. The release workflow now builds on macos-15 (arm64; macos-14 got no runner), macos-15-intel, windows-latest and ubuntu-latest, retries electron-builder's downloads (GitHub answered 504), and checks on macOS and Windows that the packaged app's tray exists, a page's notification reaches the main process and safeStorage is on the OS keychain (a round trip, plus the Keychain item on macOS and the DPAPI-wrapped key on Windows); the Windows unit tests that failed in run 42583350858 (path separators, CRLF) are fixed. Not yet: those macOS and Windows steps passing on GitHub's runners (they run only there), whether the OS then displays a notification (a hosted runner can't show it, and macOS asks the person first), and signing and notarization (no certificates; unsigned builds warn on first start and macOS cannot self-update)

items.title: Tables on your own cloud storage
items.summary: Governed lakehouse tables placed directly in the organisation's ADLS Gen2 or Blob Storage account (abfss://, wasbs://), S3 bucket or GCS bucket, not only in Cairn Store; engines get short-lived access per table and per privilege
items.done: Data stays in the organisation's own account and is still governed: Trino, Spark and pyiceberg read and write it as the person, never with a long-lived key, and an engine can reach the one table it was given, read-only unless the person may write
items.note: Cairn Catalog (catalog/src/external.rs): table and namespace locations on Azure, S3 and GCS accepted only inside registered external locations (fail closed: anything else outside Cairn Store's own places is refused, as is everything when the registrations cannot be loaded); the catalog writes its metadata files there with access for the one file's folder; with each table (load, create, staged create, renewal) it hands out access for that table's location alone, read-write only to who may write: Azure service SAS (account key) or user delegation SAS (Entra service principal from a file, or workload identity), narrowed to the table's directory on ADLS Gen2 (directory SAS) or to the container without a hierarchical namespace; S3 keys from STS AssumeRole with a session policy for the prefix (or AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity); GCS tokens downscoped with a credential access boundary; with Iceberg's renewal endpoints. Trino acts for the person: iceberg.rest-catalog.session=USER and a catalog token marked delegate exchanged (RFC 8693, /v1/oauth/tokens) for the person's own token, decided by Cairn table by table. Tested end to end against real Azurite 3.35.0 (HTTPS, production-style hosts), a real Cairn Store standing in for the customer's S3 and AWS STS, the real catalog and a real Cairn, with Trino 484 (tests/test_external_locations_e2e.py, trino job): tables created, written and read through Trino as the person on the Azure container and the S3 prefix (files there), refused without the grant and outside every location, a SAS token that reaches no other container, read-only access that cannot write or delete, S3 keys for the table's prefix only, revocations stopping new hand-outs, a service principal's user delegation SAS used by Trino; pyiceberg reading the S3 table with the person's token; the catalog's SAS signatures equal to Azure's SDK's. Still 🟡: Azurite has no hierarchical namespace or DFS endpoint, so per-table directory SAS and ADLS Gen2 itself are checked only by signature; GCS (no emulator of Google's STS) and Spark on these tables are not run; Entra, AWS STS, workload identities and Vault are not run against the real services

items.title: Storage credentials and external locations as governed objects
items.summary: Administrators register how storage is reached and where tables may live; people and groups are granted to create tables there and to read and write files
items.done: Nothing reaches the organisation's storage except through a registered location, secrets never sit in Cairn, every hand-out of access is decided and audited, and a revoked grant takes effect on the next request
items.note: cairn.dataaccess.storage_locations (migration 0137): storage credentials (Azure, S3, GCS; secrets only as file:, k8s:, vault: or workload references, configuration that looks like a secret refused) and external locations (a URL prefix and its credential; never overlapping one another or Cairn's own storage; read-only option) under /v1/storage/credentials and /v1/storage/locations (MANAGE_SYSTEM_OPERATIONS); CREATE_TABLE, READ_FILES and WRITE_FILES granted to people and groups as policies in the decision point's storage layer (urn:li:externalLocation:<name>); Cairn Catalog loads them (/v1/storage/catalog-config) and asks before each creation and each hand-out (/v1/storage/decide), every one written to the audit log (storage.create_table, storage.vend), refused when Cairn cannot be asked; files by path with READ_FILES/WRITE_FILES (GET /v1/locations/credentials on the catalog). Registry kinds storage_credentials, external_locations, external_location_grants (bundles, Terraform, export, forms); External locations and Storage credentials tabs in the Lakehouse hub with demo samples. Tested: tests/test_storage_locations.py (references, overlaps, the policy layer, the catalog's questions, the API) and end to end in tests/test_external_locations_e2e.py (grants, refusals, revocations and the audit log through Trino and the real catalog)

items.title: System tables
items.summary: Cairn's operational data as SQL tables in Trino (cairn_system): the audit log, refused access, query history, costs, lineage, warehouse usage and job runs, with documented schemas
items.done: People and operators answer "my most expensive queries this week", "who read this table", "what failed last night" in SQL, from any tool that speaks Trino, under the same policies as every other table
items.note: cairn.dataaccess.system_tables (no migration): eight Iceberg tables materialised by the scheduler's leader every CAIRN_SYSTEM_TABLES_INTERVAL_SECONDS (60) into a Cairn Catalog of their own (CAIRN_SYSTEM_TABLES_CATALOG), read by Trino as cairn_system with a read-only catalog token: audit.events, access.decisions (explicit denies, from the audit log), query.history (user, statement, sha256 and fingerprint, tables, times, bytes, warehouse, price), billing.usage (per day: a person's queries per warehouse, tables, teams, engine runs, AI usage), lineage.table_lineage and lineage.column_lineage (tables' upstream lineage and jobs' inputs and outputs, Trino's included), compute.warehouse_events (usage reports, starts), jobs.runs (flows, jobs, SQL workflows). Append tables by key with a watermark kept on each snapshot; recomputed tables replaced only when their content changes; synced_at on every row and Iceberg snapshots as the change feed. Chosen over a PostgreSQL connector on Cairn's database: Trino gets no database credentials, lineage and team costs (not in the database) are there, history outlives the sources, and it works on any Cairn database. Governance in TrinoAccess on top of the policies: reading needs VIEW_DATASET_PROFILE like any table; user_name tables show a person their own rows unless MANAGE_SYSTEM_OPERATIONS; statement and error redacted without VIEW_QUERY_TEXT; read-only for everyone; a missing decision filters and masks (fail closed). Freshness within the interval plus 60 s; retention CAIRN_SYSTEM_TABLES_RETENTION_DAYS (90) and per table with PUT /v1/system-tables/<schema>/<table>/retention (operators, audited, deletes at once); GET /v1/system-tables, POST /v1/system-tables/sync; each table in the catalog with its description and column descriptions (also Iceberg comments, shown by Trino); a System tables list in the SQL workspace. Tested end to end (tests/test_system_tables_e2e.py, trino job): real Trino 484, Cairn Store and two Cairn Catalogs; queries, a refused read, a flow run, posted costs, AI usage, a warehouse report and a CTAS's lineage, then every table through Trino: rows within the documented bound, an operator sees all with SQL, a person only theirs with SQL masked (and filtering on it finds nothing), someone without a grant refused and the tables hidden, writes, deletes, drops and schema creation refused for all, the user guide's examples, catalog descriptions, retention deleting and later syncs appending nothing twice; plus tests/test_system_tables.py (decisions, fail-closed, definitions) and vitest for the list. Not yet: the Helm chart does not deploy it (the second Cairn Catalog, Trino's cairn_system catalog file and the setting on the API and scheduler are configured by hand, as administration.md shows)

items.title: Split control plane and data plane
items.summary: Cairn (API, UI, catalog metadata, PDP, gateway) hosted; Trino, Spark, jobs, flows' steps in the customer's cluster on the customer's storage; per workspace `compute: customer
items.done: managed`
items.note: The control plane reaches data-plane compute only through an outbound tunnel the data plane opens; Trino there asks the hosted PDP; the tunnel down, a forged or a revoked data plane are refused; Cairn never holds the storage keys

items.title: Network controls for user code, and private networking
items.summary: Admin-set egress allowlist for jobs, notebooks, sandboxes, flows' steps and agent apps; private endpoints and internal load balancers in the cloud modules
items.done: With egress enforced, user code reaches only Cairn, the lakehouse and what an admin allowed; every refusal is logged; object storage and the Cairn API can be reached privately
items.note: cairn.network (migration 0136): /v1/network/egress-rules (hosts, *.domain, CIDRs, ports, per workspace or all; check; cairn_egress_rule; Trust & security › Network egress); CAIRN_EGRESS_ENFORCE fails closed. Cairn's egress proxy (cairn egress-proxy, docker/egress-proxy.Dockerfile, standard library only): CONNECT and HTTP to what the run's Cairn-signed credential allows, names resolved once and connected by address, private addresses only by CIDR rule (or CAIRN_EGRESS_ALLOW_PRIVATE), the metadata address never, TLS server name must match (no domain fronting), every refusal one JSON line (egress.denied). Kubernetes: per-workspace NetworkPolicy applied before each run with the chart's Role (DNS, Cairn's namespace, CIDR rules), pods labelled, proxy env; agent apps' pods get the egress policy (Kubernetes only when enforced); sandboxes add the rules to their allowed hosts and log refusals; chart cairn.egress (proxy Deployment, key Secret). Docker: runs join only an internal network the proxy also joins. Terraform private_networking in modules/aws (S3 gateway endpoint, bucket limited to it, internal NLB/ALB, PrivateLink endpoint service), gcp (Private Service Connect for Google APIs and a private DNS zone, internal LB, PSC service attachment), azure (Private Endpoints for blob and dfs with private DNS zones, internal LB, Private Link service); examples take it. Tested: a real job container and the real proxy container (tests/test_egress_e2e.py, trino job: allowed host reached, other refused and logged, no way around the proxy, nothing outside with no rule), real sockets (tests/test_egress.py), terraform fmt and tflint here. Written for CI only: the NetworkPolicy on kind (tests/test_egress_kind.py, spark-kind job; kindnet enforces NetworkPolicy since kind v0.24) and terraform validate of the modules and examples (job terraform-modules; the providers were too large to download here). They pass in CI (job spark-kind). Not yet: applies on AWS, GCP and Azure accounts, the egress proxy as a Docker Compose service

items.title: Everything as code, with no configuration gaps
items.summary: Every route that changes something is configuration (a resource type), an action, or not configuration for a stated reason; the settings APIs are types too; the licence is set by the platform's Terraform module
items.done: Nothing a team configures is left to clicks: a new API that changes something and is not classified fails CI, and "why is this not in Terraform?" has a written answer per route
items.note: 78 resource types (17 new): agent_pools (PUT/DELETE /agents/pools/{name} added; an occupied pool is refused), persona_grants (GET /governance/personas/{id}/grants), token_domains (created once, only forgotten), api_limits, bucket_quotas (GET /storage/v1/quotas), system_table_retention, data_contracts, product_request_policies (GET /marketplace/policies, DELETE …/products/{urn}/policy), sql_shares (GET /sql/shares), feature_tables (DELETE /v1/ml/feature-tables/{name}: out of the catalog, no longer served), online_feature_tables (GET /v1/ml/online-feature-tables), model_monitors (GET /v1/ml/monitors), agent_trace_settings, playbooks, desktop_policy, ui_settings, extensions (token and signing secret kept as installed); dashboards carry their actions (saved with the dashboard, matched by name, deleted with it), input tables their reviewers (in place), flows their editors and viewers; contract-made quality monitors are the contract's. The gate (tests/test_iac_coverage.py) classifies all 585 changing routes: 185 calls of a type, 9 on COVERED_BY, 195 actions (each with its reason), 196 excluded by category (runtime state 49, credential 50, workflow 50, data 23, release 14, identity provider 8, deployment 2: the licence, deploy/terraform/modules/cairn); an action can never be created and deleted. modules/cairn: licence (sensitive) or licence_file, licence_required, licence_tenant_id make the Secret <release>-licence the chart reads; tenant_licences per hosted tenant (examples/hetzner uses it). Tested: the gate; bundles (tests/test_iac_roundtrip.py: 58 runnable types made, exported, planned with no changes, changed in place, pruned; a persona's grants and a query's shares by their parents' ids); real Terraform with the provider built from source (tests/test_terraform_provider.py: every runnable type created, no drift, changed in place, imported, destroyed; the id-referencing ones through references; an exported workspace imported with no changes); bucket quotas, online feature tables and system table retention on real Cairn Store and Catalog, checked in the store's admin API, by an online lookup and in the table's properties (tests/test_iac_lake_e2e.py, job terraform); input-table reviewers on real Trino (tests/test_trino_e2e.py); the module's licence by terraform test with mocked providers, fmt, tflint and validate of modules/cairn and examples/kind (job terraform-modules; examples/hetzner validates in CI only: its hcloud provider is not reachable here). Not covered here: cloud applies of the AWS, GCP, Azure and Hetzner modules need accounts (L125 stays 🟡 for that); the kind apply does not install a licence (no signed test licence for the image)

items.title: Orchestrate across platforms, from Cairn Flows and from Airflow
items.summary: Flow steps for any REST API, Databricks, Snowflake and BigQuery; a flow with them exports to Airflow with Airflow's own providers; Airflow starts Cairn flows and waits for them
items.done: A flow calls a partner API and polls it, runs a Databricks job, Snowflake SQL and a BigQuery job, with credentials only from secret scopes (read as the owner, never in the flow or its logs), TLS verified, egress rules applied and remote work cancelled with the run; the same flow runs in Airflow on its providers; a DAG drives a Cairn flow, fails with it and cancels it when killed
items.note: cairn.flows.platforms (no migration): step types http (method, URL, headers, a JSON body with templates, bearer/basic/header auth from a scope, a private CA from the scope, accepted statuses, a JSONPath kept as steps.x.result, polling a status URL from the answer or Location to success/failure values), databricks (Jobs API 2.2 run-now with job parameters or runs/submit, PAT or OAuth M2M, the run page, idempotency token), snowflake (SQL API v2, key-pair JWT with an optional passphrase, async statement handle, EXECUTE TASK), bigquery (a service account's token, jobs.insert with Cairn's job id, jobs.get, results); one core (secrets read as the owner and scrubbed from every message, TLS always verified, through the egress proxy when enforced, otherwise link-local addresses always and private ones unless CAIRN_FLOWS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS refused, fail closed); waiting parks the run; cancel and time out cancel the remote work (engine hooks, for-each too). Publishing refuses a scope the owner cannot read; definitions refuse credential headers and credentials in URLs. Canvas: a Platforms group with forms whose fields appear as they apply. Export: HttpOperator/HttpSensor (a task group), DatabricksRunNowOperator/DatabricksSubmitRunOperator, SnowflakeSqlApiOperator, BigQueryInsertJobOperator, named Airflow connections described in the file, no secrets. cairn-airflow-provider: CairnFlowRunOperator (deferrable via CairnFlowRunTrigger, fails with the run, cancels it on kill through the trigger's and the operator's on_kill) and CairnFlowRunSensor. Example examples/flows/cross-platform.yaml. Tested: the http step against a real HTTP service in a container over TLS with a private CA, polling, three kinds of auth, failures, and egress allowed and refused through the real egress proxy (tests/test_flows_http_e2e.py); a real Airflow 3.3 driving a real Cairn: deferred and polled runs, a sensor, a failing flow, a kill cancelling the run deferred and on a worker, and the exported DAG imported with no errors with the pinned providers (http 6.1.0, databricks 7.20.0, snowflake 6.17.0, google 22.5.0) (tests/test_flows_airflow_platforms_e2e.py); Databricks, Snowflake and BigQuery request and response handling, cancels, failures and fail-closed secrets against stand-ins with the documented API shapes (tests/test_flows_platforms.py); vitest for the forms. Written for CI only: bigquery against the real emulator (tests/test_flows_bigquery_e2e.py, ghcr.io/goccy/bigquery-emulator:0.6.6, which could not be pulled here: its registry's blob host is refused). Not yet: Databricks and Snowflake against real accounts (they have no emulators and there are no accounts here), BigQuery on Google Cloud itself

items.title: People & roles
items.summary: One administrator's section for who is in Cairn, what roles they hold and why: people and groups from SCIM, single sign-on or made in Cairn, a person's page, effective access with the policies behind it, people and groups as code for deployments without SCIM
items.done: An administrator finds a person, sees their attributes, groups, personas with why (direct, group, attribute rule, grant), what they can see, workspaces, agents they own, last sign-in, open access reviews and recent audit; asks "can this person do this to this asset?" and gets yes or no with the policy, persona or purpose that decided it; makes and deactivates people and groups without SCIM (sessions end), with SCIM's refused; all audited and declarable in Terraform
items.note: cairn.identity.people, migration 0138 (cairn_people): /v1/people/users (search, paging, filters status, source scim/manual/sso, group, type person/service), a person's page and .../access (what they can see, by persona scope and the purposes that restrict them), /v1/people/groups and members, /v1/people/principals (agent identities with owner and scopes, workload identities, Cairn's own accounts), POST /v1/people/access-check (the policy engine's decision with explain, labelled by persona and purpose, the personas that did not apply and why, never written as the person's deny). MANAGE_POLICIES for every call, never by agent credentials; Cairn Core unreadable is a 503. Manual people are written to Cairn Core as the provisioning account (attributes as io.cairn.* structured properties, declared by the control plane), manual groups are native (single sign-on never overwrites them); SCIM people and groups are refused (409); SSO people can be adopted and deactivated; deactivation suspends in Core and ends every Cairn session (the SCIM path). Resource types people, people_groups, people_group_members (Terraform cairn_person, cairn_group, cairn_group_member, forms generated). UI: People & roles (/people, admins only) with People, Groups, Roles, Service accounts & agents and Access check, a person drawer, palette entries, help. Tested here: the API on Cairn's real services, policy engine and database (tests/test_people.py), bundles and export (tests/test_iac_roundtrip.py), Terraform create, drift, update, import and destroy (tests/test_terraform_provider.py), vitest, the built UI in Chromium: people → person → why, two access checks, a person made with the form and deactivated, a non-admin refused (tests/test_people_ui_e2e.py), axe on six People & roles views and its form (tests/test_accessibility_e2e.py). Only in CI's stack job (Cairn Core does not run here): the same against Cairn Core itself, with structured properties, native membership and suspension read back from Core (tests/e2e/test_people_live.py)

items.title: Managed Postgres
items.summary: PostgreSQL instances run by Cairn per team or workload (like Lakebase, Snowflake Postgres or RDS): size, standbys with automatic failover, pooling, allow-listed parameters, maintenance windows; continuous backups to Cairn Store, point-in-time restore and branches from a time or a backup; status, metrics and slow queries
items.done: A team gets a PostgreSQL instance it can rely on: it survives losing its primary, it can be restored to any second of its retention (data before the time, none after), every backup is checked by a restore, no secret is on a command line or shown, and the SRE agent and dashboards read its health from Cairn's API
items.note: cairn.databases (migration 0140): instances (/v1/databases/instances, cairn_pg_instances, CREATE_DATABASE_INSTANCE, MANAGE_DATABASE_INSTANCE, VIEW_DATABASE_INSTANCE, USE_DATABASE_INSTANCE on urn:li:pgInstance:<name>); L88's databases live on them (instance), the server given before is the instance default (health and metrics only). Runtimes: CloudNativePG 1.27.0 on Kubernetes (cairn.databases.cnpg: a Cluster with 1 + replicas pods and anti-affinity, Pooler, Barman Cloud WAL archiving and base backups, ScheduledBackup, Backup, recovery bootstrap for restores, switchover through the cluster's status, the operator's exporter scraped) and Docker (cairn.databases.docker_runtime: PostgreSQL container plus a standard-library sidecar on a network of their own; archive_command succeeds only once the WAL file is in the store; pg_basebackup uploaded by the sidecar; TLS, data checksums, pg_stat_statements; fixed ports). Allow-listed, checked parameters; minor upgrades and restarts in the maintenance window (pending, apply-pending); resize; schedules with retention (expired base backups and the WAL before the oldest kept deleted, the newest always kept) and restore checks; point-in-time restore into a new instance (databases renamed or dropped, logins never carried, a password of its own, its own first backup); a database branch {"at"} or {"backup"}; status (health with problems), metrics, slow-queries for the SRE agent (L142) and dashboards (L143); superuser passwords derived from CAIRN_PG_INSTANCE_KEY, never stored. Chart cairn.databases.instances (API and scheduler settings; pg-kubernetes.yaml Role for CloudNativePG's kinds in the instances' namespace only). Kinds postgres_instances, postgres_parameters, postgres_backup_schedules (provider and forms regenerated); Postgres instances tab in Compute & jobs (create form, status, backups, schedules, restore to a point in time, parameters, metrics, slow statements; palette entry). Tested on real components: Docker runtime with PostgreSQL 16 containers and a real Cairn Store binary (tests/test_postgres_instances.py, trino job: create, TLS, databases and logins, parameters with a restart, a backup in the store and its restore check, point-in-time restore with the rows before the time and not after, the source's logins and password refused, a branch from a backup, metrics and slow queries, resize and a new image keeping data and port, retention, the default instance); bundles and real Terraform for instances and parameters (tests/test_iac_roundtrip.py, tests/test_terraform_provider.py); vitest and a browser check of the tab. Written for CI only (pods cannot run here): tests/test_postgres_cnpg_kind.py (spark-kind job: the pinned operator, an instance with a standby and a pooler made with the chart's Role, a backup to a Cairn Store in the cluster, writes continuing after the primary pod is deleted, a restore into a new instance). The CloudNativePG kind test passes in CI (job spark-kind: a standby promoted after the primary is lost, a backup to the store and a restore). Not yet: restore checks and scheduled-backup bookkeeping on Kubernetes (the operator's own; checks are Docker-only), major upgrades by import (documented, not automated), storage growth on Docker (volumes are not limited), and backup schedules in the Terraform test (it has no store)

items.title: End-to-end observability for the whole platform
items.summary: OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and logs from every component, the bundled open-source stack or the customer's own backend, and one view in Cairn that follows a request across components and ties metrics, logs, traces, SLOs, alerts and incidents together
items.done: A request through Cairn's API to Trino (and the PDP) is one trace visible in Cairn with spans from several processes, its logs found by trace id; an SLO burns, its alert fires and reaches a notification route, an incident opens with what changed around it; no secret or masked value in anything exported
items.note: cairn.observability (migration 0140: cairn_obs_config, cairn_obs_alerts, cairn_obs_incidents, cairn_obs_incident_events, cairn_obs_deploys). Telemetry (telemetry, standard OTEL_*, sampling, headers from Secrets or a file; the otel extra is in the image): FastAPI, httpx, SQLAlchemy, the core proxy, workers; Trino queries carry traceparent and a cairn_trace client tag; flow steps are spans linked to the request that started the run; jobs get TRACEPARENT; Spark runs are linked through their OpenLineage run id; x-trace-id on every answer. Redaction (redact) on every span and log record before export, fail closed (dropped and counted): headers, credential-named attributes, query values, route templates for paths, key-shaped path segments, SQL literals, tokens/JWTs/keys in text. Bundled stack (deploy/observability/stack, Collector 0.163.2 Apache-2.0 with span metrics, service graph and a second redaction including Trino's key in its OPA URLs; Prometheus 3.15.1 Apache-2.0; Loki 3.6.18 and Tempo 2.9.5 AGPL-3.0): Helm cairn.observability.enabled (off by default; Trino tracing, the OpenTelemetry Java agent 2.32.0 for Cairn Core and its web app, network policies, optional persistence) and the Compose overlay (also Airflow's OTel). In Cairn (/v1/observability, MANAGE_SYSTEM_OPERATIONS): health map, journeys (Tempo; links for vendors), logs by trace or component (Loki), SLOs with multi-window burn-rate alerts, PromQL/LogQL alert rules, silences, acknowledgements, routing to the existing notification routes, incidents with a timeline of alerts, notes and the audit log's changes, IaC change requests and deploys, and /incidents/{id}/context for the SRE agent (L142). Resource types observability_slos, observability_alert_rules, observability_silences (Terraform cairn_observability_*, forms). UI: Observability (/observability, operators) with Health, Request journey (waterfall), Logs, SLOs (budget, burn), Alerts (rules, silences) and Incidents, palette entries, help. items.title: An SRE agent for operations and managed Postgres
items.summary: A built-in agent identity with read-mostly scopes that investigates incidents (by itself or when asked) and managed PostgreSQL instances through Cairn's own APIs, writes findings with their evidence, ranks causes, proposes remediations people approve, and drafts postmortems
items.done: On-call people get the investigation done for them (what changed, what the metrics, logs, traces and the database show, with the queries and results cited) and decide on concrete remediations with one click that runs as them; the agent can never apply anything, and with no model, no gateway or a failing tool it says so and does nothing
items.note: cairn.sre (migration 0142: cairn_sre_config, cairn_sre_runs, cairn_sre_actions, cairn_sre_postmortems): the agent agt_sre_agent (agent hub: pause and quotas apply) with scopes read, model, iac:propose; each run a 15-minute credential for the person it acts for (who asks, or the settings' run_as when it joins an incident of an auto_join severity by itself), revoked at the end; every tool call through Cairn's API in process with that credential (scope checks, the person's permissions, audit). Tools: the incident's context, PromQL and LogQL (/v1/observability/alert-rules/test, now a read-only POST), logs, traces, journeys, health, SLO status, deploys; a managed instance's status, metrics, slow statements, backups; the Postgres helper (cairn.sre.pghelper: slow statements planned with EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN) on a short-lived read login (L88) dropped after the diagnosis, index suggestions with the plan as evidence, vacuum and dead-tuple hints, connection saturation and idle transactions, replication lag, WAL archiving, cache hit ratio, backup freshness, each with a remediation); read-only diagnostic SQL (one statement, read-only transaction, 5 s, 50 rows); notes (finding/hypothesis/note marked as the agent's, each keeping the cited calls' tool, input and result), ranked causes, change requests (L126) and runbook actions from an allow-list (restart_instance, switchover_instance, backup_instance, silence_alert, rerun_flow) recorded as pending. Approve (POST /v1/sre/actions/<id>/approve) runs it as the approver through the API with their credentials (a change request approved and applied through /v1/iac/changes with its own rules); refusals leave it pending and are audited. Ask the SRE agent (incident chat), Diagnose on an instance (/v1/sre/instances/<name>/diagnose, no model needed for the report), postmortems drafted on resolve (timeline, impact from SLO budgets, actions, cause, fix, follow-ups) that a person edits and approves. Fail closed: no model, no gateway, paused or over budget, a model call refused, a tool failing: said in the incident, nothing done. Kinds sre_runbooks (alert-label matchers, diagnostic steps, allowed actions), sre_agent_settings (enabled, auto_join, run_as, model, max steps, tokens per run, runs a day) and postgres_indexes (/v1/databases/<name>/indexes, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, MANAGE_DATABASE), provider regenerated. UI: the incident drawer's SRE agent panel (Investigate, proposals with evidence, Approve/Reject, chat, postmortem editor), Evidence under the agent's notes in the timeline, Diagnose on the Postgres instance page, a palette entry; docs (administration, *SRE agent*). Found and fixed on the way: pg_stat_statements kept the CREATE ROLE ... PASSWORD of every database login, so slow statements showed login passwords (now not recorded, and masked in the API and in redaction); a note's evidence could be cut mid-JSON by redaction; an incident was announced before its alert was linked. Tested on real components (tests/test_sre_agent_e2e.py, trino job, its own pytest): the bundled stack's Collector, Prometheus, Loki and Tempo, a managed PostgreSQL 16 instance on Docker with the store, the real AI gateway in front of the deterministic stand-in model: an application's spans on a 400,000-row table without an index make a PromQL latency alert fire and open an incident; the agent joins by itself, runs the matching runbook first, diagnoses with EXPLAIN on a read login, writes a finding citing that evidence, ranks causes and proposes a postgres_indexes change request; with its own credential it cannot approve or apply it, restart, or build the index; someone without the privileges is refused; the approver's approval builds the index as them, the statement is fast, the alert resolves, the postmortem is drafted, edited and approved; filled connections (idle in transaction) give a proposed restart, refused without MANAGE_DATABASE_INSTANCE, run as the approver and the slots freed; Diagnose with a question; no model, a model the gateway does not serve and a stopped Loki each said in the incident with nothing proposed; no password, provider key or token in anything it wrote. Chromium (tests/test_sre_ui_e2e.py): a cited finding's evidence, a proposal approved and run as the operator, a backup refused to someone without the privilege, axe on the incident with the panel; vitest. Not yet: the real model's quality (the live-model variant in tests/test_live_model.py passes with the stand-in here; it runs on the real model only in the live-model job), switchover_instance (Kubernetes only) and rerun_flow approved end to end, a slow PDP as an injected fault, and diagnosis on the CloudNativePG runtime

items.title: Snowflake and Databricks tables in place
items.summary: Snowflake and Databricks tables read where they are, governed by Cairn's policy decision point like lakehouse tables: Snowflake Open Catalog, Snowflake-managed Iceberg (Horizon) and Unity Catalog through their Iceberg REST endpoints (zero copy), live federated queries on Snowflake through Trino's Snowflake connector, and Databricks Delta Sharing as a recipient. Ring: Extend (Trino reads them) and Activate (they are catalogued and kept in step). Reads: grants, masks (column labels), row filters and policies on the tables' URNs; the registering operator's secret scopes. Writes back: each table as a snowflake or databricks dataset in Cairn Core with its schema, owner and domain; lineage when a Cairn table is made from one (Trino's OpenLineage) and from a shared table to the table it lands in; syncs and registrations audited. Governance: MANAGE_SYSTEM_OPERATIONS to register, MANAGE_INGESTION to list and sync, WRITE_DATASET on a Delta Sharing target; Trino asks Cairn about every table (VIEW_DATASET_PROFILE, WRITE_DATASET, …); read-only unless registered writable; a decision that cannot be made, a credential that cannot be read or a missing credential target refuses. Visibility: the tables in the Catalog under their warehouse's platform, with lineage; Lakehouse › External catalogs leads with a card per warehouse

items.title: Apache NiFi: governed data connectors
items.summary: Managed NiFi 2 deployments per team and environment, run by Cairn from the unmodified upstream image (apache/nifi, Apache-2.0), reached only through Cairn, with flows kept in Cairn and deployed by it: NiFi's 300+ processors next to Cairn's own loaders. Ring: Extend (a runtime that registers back) and Activate (connectors that keep the graph alive). Reads: the owner's secret scopes, the lakehouse decisions on the sink's table (write, and no mask or filter for the owner), the deployment's team and domain. Writes back: each flow a dataFlow (nifi) with its owner, the team as technical owner and its domain; its process groups dataJobs with the datasets their processors read and write (database tables, topics, buckets, folders, Iceberg tables) plus declared lineage and the lakehouse table, so source → table shows on the asset page; activity windows (status counters, bulletins) as OpenLineage run events (Core's runs) and runs of nifi:<flow> in pipeline observability; every change audited. Governance: CREATE_NIFI_DEPLOYMENT; VIEW_NIFI_DEPLOYMENT, DEPLOY_NIFI_FLOW, MANAGE_NIFI_DEPLOYMENT on urn:li:nifiDeployment:<name>, decided for every canvas request through Cairn's proxy (deny by default, refused when undecidable); only a flow's owner changes it; the sink writes as the owner through a lakehouse session (hourly tokens, per-table vended keys), never a store key. Visibility: Ingestion › Connectors (NiFi); each flow a pipeline in the Catalog with lineage to its table; its runs in Runs
items.done: A team gets a NiFi it does not run and nobody reaches except through Cairn (TLS with a CA Cairn pins, one user whose password only Cairn derives, the canvas proxied with a decision per request); a flow defined as code is deployed by Cairn with its sensitive parameters from secret scopes (never in the definition, NiFi's export, a log, an environment or a command line) and lands records in a lakehouse table as its owner, governed like any table (masks apply when others read it); the flow, its groups, lineage and runs are in Cairn Core and pipeline observability; deployments scale and are deleted cleanly; everything as code and in the UI's forms
